description: A call of the mesh's own tools that starts a subagent on a host of the mesh, or messages a chat there: drawn like a subagent's row (a state mark, its title over its host and model, a › at the right), the whole line opening that chat; once the chat answers, its answer sits under the card in a bubble of its own. Never folded into a ToolGroup.
opens: A call of mcp__mesh__start_subagent or mcp__mesh__message_chat

parts.name: frame
parts.shows: The tool-card border (1px rule colour, 8px corners) round the head line and anything opened under it, with no padding of its own. Border red on error, amber while asking permission.

parts.name: head line
parts.shows: Padding 7px/10px, items 10px apart: the mark, then two stacked lines filling the width, then the toggles, then a › chevron (75% opacity) when there's a chat to open. Under the pointer, when openable, the line lights up (text colour at 5%) and the pointer is a hand.

parts.name: mark
parts.shows: 16px: a spinner while the call runs or the chat it started is working or waiting on a question; ✓ (success green) when done; ✕ (error red) on error, or when the chat ended badly (its claude exited, its host went, the wait ran out, it was interrupted); a grey stop icon when interrupted. Invisible (its space kept) while the call asks permission.

parts.name: title
parts.shows: Bold, ellipsized: for start_subagent the started chat's title as its host lists it, else the title given, else the first 60 characters of the prompt, else "Subagent"; for message_chat the chat's Bot's name, else its title, else "Chat <first 8 of its id>".

parts.name: subtitle
parts.shows: Caption size, dimmed, ellipsized, parts joined by " · ": "Subagent on <host>" (or "Subagent") then the model's display name if known; or "Messaged on <host>" (or "Messaged"). Then at most one of: "interrupted", "the wait ran out", "denied", "waiting for an answer", "still working" / "stopped waiting for it", "not waited for", "its claude exited (<code>)", "its host went before it answered".
text: its host went before it answered

parts.name: toggles
parts.shows: Small toggle buttons as on a tool card: "Prompt" (start_subagent) or "Message" (message_chat) opens what it was given; "Output"/"Error" only when the result wasn't the mesh's normal reply.

actions.does: Opens that chat in the main area, as the sidebar opens a mesh chat. If it isn't listed here yet: a toast "<title>: its chat isn't listed here yet" plus " (is <host> reachable from here?)" once the call is over.
Tooltip "Open this chat on <host>", or "This chat on <host> isn't listed here yet".

parts.name: opened sections
parts.shows: The prompt/message and any output open under the head line inside the frame, 10px in from each side, as wide as the card, 8px below.

parts.name: answer
parts.shows: Outside and under the frame (6px gap): a bubble on the raised fill (12px corners, 8px/12px padding) with the chat's answer as markdown. If the chat hadn't finished, a dimmed (60%) line "What it had said so far" heads it.
text: What it had said so far

states.name: starting / running
states.shows: Spinner; the chat it is starting is found among the host's chats by its title, so the line opens it even before the reply.

states.name: chat working or waiting
states.shows: After the call returns, the mark follows the chat's own state as its host lists it: spinner while it works, "waiting for an answer" when it waits on a question.

states.name: failed / refused
states.shows: A result that isn't the mesh's reply is shown as a normal card's Error; ✕ and red border.

states.name: asking permission
states.shows: Amber border, mark hidden, buttons inside the frame at the bottom (see PermissionPrompt).

states.name: jumped to
states.shows: Accent tint flash over the frame.
